source.title: ENCHTABLE: Unified Safety Alignment Transfer in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models
source.authors: Jia-Lin Wu; Ke-Cen Li; Zhi-Cong Huang; Xin-Feng Li; Xiaofeng Wang; Cheng Hong

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmful-response rates in downstream fine-tuned models, including a LoRA fine-tuning condition, using safety datasets. This bears conceptually on benign fine-tuning and safety erosion, but it does not replicate a controlled before-and-after fine-tuning experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports harmful fine-tuning of a surrogate to construct a safety vector, but that training is deliberately used to induce harmful behavior and is not a test of naturally occurring safety loss. It evaluates jailbreak attacks, but does not test compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. Table 4's flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of its individual unsafe-rate values.
record.test_reason: This is a mitigation-method paper, but it reports how often fine-tuned models give harmful responses. Two of its results are matched before-and-after comparisons on benign fine-tuning. In Table 5, LLaMA3-8B-Instruct LoRA-tuned on Code290k-ShareGPT has an average unsafe rate of 0.273, against 0.030 for the Instruct model. In Table 8, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B goes from 0.285 to 0.628 on DGQ after Japanese reasoning fine-tuning. The main downstream models (Tables 1, 2 and 4) are downloaded checkpoints compared with LLaMA3-8B-Instruct rather than with their own pre-fine-tuning weights. The jailbreak results measure the authors' defence, not prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that ENCHTABLE transfers safety to fine-tuned models across domains and architectures with little utility loss, and outperforms baselines under normal and jailbreak settings. They also take as given, citing Qi et al., that fine-tuning degrades safety alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes NTK-constrained harmful fine-tuning of a surrogate to extract a safety vector, then merges that vector into task models; this is not a reproduction of the original fine-tuning-safety-loss method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that unsafe rate and utility vary with scaling coefficient β and surrogate harmful fine-tuning steps T; safety also varies with surrogate choice (Base versus Instruct), domain, and attack type.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 4, downstream fine-tuned models show higher unsafe rates than LLaMA3-8B-Instruct under static jailbreaks. For example, they often exceed 0.4 on writing-style mutations, and exceed 0.8 vs about 0.6 for Instruct under Misrepresentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuned downstream models are more susceptible to semantic or persuasion jailbreaks than their aligned counterparts.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (2026)
record.problems: The main downstream SFT results lack matched pre-fine-tuning checkpoints, limiting causal conclusions about safety erosion. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Jailbreak results are mainly figure-based, and the text gives only grouped descriptions rather than individual attack values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's Qwen2.5 and Mistral unsafe-rate cells were omitted because the flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of each value to a model and metric. Figure 4's individual attack-by-domain bars were not separately extracted; the retained rows follow the grouped descriptions in §5.6.

untested.parts: The surrogate is harmful-fine-tuned on 1,000 BeaverTails pairs to build the safety vector, but its unsafe rate is never reported. Figure 3 only says that too few steps leave it insufficiently harmful.
Carefully chosen benign data is not tested. Only ordinary code and Japanese reasoning data are used, in matched comparisons.
No per-token KL divergence or position-wise analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding attack is applied to measure bypass. SafeDecoding is used only as a defence baseline.
The Attention and FFN variants of the defence both work, but neither is a localization test of where safety resides.

missing.what: Benign fine-tuning in a matched pair: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (Bound) has a DGQ unsafe rate of 0.285, and the Japanese-tuned SFT model has 0.628.
SFT-model bars for Instruct vs SFT under the ten jailbreaks, for context on fine-tuned models' susceptibility. Values are figure-only, with grouped descriptions in the text.
Unsafe rates of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (avg 0.324) and OpenHermes2.5-Mistral-7B (avg 0.648) downstream SFT models, with no matched pre-fine-tuning baseline.

record.verdict_notes: The main downstream models are compared against LLaMA3-8B-Instruct rather than their own parents, so only Table 5 and Table 8 give clean benign-fine-tuning comparisons. Judges differ by experiment: MD-Judge-v0.2 for the safety sets, the SorryBench judge for mutations, and a refusal-keyword PatternScore for ICA/DRA. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: It uses harmful fine-tuning to build a safety vector, but does not report whether harmful fine-tuning itself removes refusal on the surrogate.

No matched pre-fine-tuning checkpoint is evaluated for the main downstream models, and the study does not isolate ordinary benign data from other differences between models. It does not test carefully chosen benign data separately.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base output-distribution comparison is measured.
It tests several jailbreak attack types, but not compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or whether any bypass works by getting past early response tokens.
The attention and FFN variants are not a test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study does not test why safety would be shallow or attribute shallowness to training data or objectives.
The study does not train safety to be deeper than the first tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: Code-LLaMA3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured unsafe-response rate on safety datasets for the downloaded downstream SFT model.

conditions.value: SAD, CAQ, DGQ, HMQ; aggregate reported in Table 1

rows.note: Aggregate across safety datasets; the paper reports the downstream SFT model's rate but does not give a matched pre-fine-tuning rate for this model.
rows.check: The baseline is LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, not this model's own pre-fine-tuning checkpoint. Code-LLaMA3-8B is described as built on the LLaMA-3-8B architecture, so it may never have been safety-aligned. 0.802 vs 0.030 cannot be read as erosion, and 'partial' is wrong in any case given the size of the gap.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reported downstream SFT models and the LoRA fine-tuning condition
reader_labels.reason: Unsafe rates are reported after fine-tuning and are high relative to the paper's safety threshold, but there is no matched before-fine-tuning measurement to establish the size or cause of an increase (R1-R8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested static and dynamic jailbreak attacks on downstream models
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports unsafe responses under jailbreak attacks, including elevated rates for downstream models and improvements after ENCHTABLE; this supports only the general jailbreak-bypass aspect, not the specified opening-token mechanism (R9-R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ENCHTABLE-treated models under the reported attack groups
reader_labels.reason: The text describes reduced but not uniformly absent unsafe responses for the attack groups, and reports near-zero rates only for ICA and DRA; it does not establish that the specific prefilling, suffix, or decoding bypasses are effective (R9-R16).
